name: Vatican City
summary_text: Vatican City is workable for trans visitors — and an unusual case: it is a 0.49 km² tourist enclave (museums, basilica, square) with essentially no resident jurisdiction a traveler can fall afoul of. Nothing about being trans is criminalised; there are no bathrooms inspections, no morality police, and the Swiss Guards and gendarmerie do not police tourist gender expression. Millions of tourists of every presentation visit annually without incident; entry is via Rome with no border formality. The doctrinal climate is hostile: the 2024 declaration "Infinite Dignity" condemned gender-affirming surgery and "gender theory" as violations of human dignity, and there is obviously no legal recognition or protection of any kind. But this is a climate signal, not a traveler-facing mechanism — the realistic worst case for a visitor is being refused entry to the basilica over a dress-code dispute (shoulders/knees rules apply to everyone). Caveat: very small population — the evidence base is thin, so this assessment carries greater-than-usual uncertainty.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 401); the underlying Reuters report (April 2024) covers the Vatican's document 'Dignitas Infinita' saying no to sex changes and 'gender theory'.

AP (Apr 2024): 'Vatican blasts gender-affirming surgery, surrogacy and gender theory as violations of human dignity' — the 'Infinite Dignity' doctrine puts transition-related care and surrogacy on a par with abortion and euthanasia.

AP News: Pope Francis endorsed same-sex civil unions in the documentary 'Francesco' (2020) - a landmark statement from the pontiff that gay couples deserve legal protection in civil-union laws (page largely navigation content at fetch time).

sources.title: Vatican blocks appointment of gay diplomat | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (Oct 2008): the Vatican blocked the appointment of a gay French diplomat (Jean-Loup Kuhn-Delforge, in a civil pact) as envoy to the Holy See, also rejecting a divorced candidate - 'The Roman Catholic Church is opposed to gay rights and any attempts to protect or recognise gay relationships in law.'

Crux (June 2021): in a historic first, the Vatican invoked its sovereign status under the 1929 treaty with Italy to protest a draft Italian anti-homophobia law via a formal nota verbale from the Secretariat of State, objecting that it could restrict the church's religious freedom.

Vatican Congregation for Catholic Education (2019): 'Male and Female He Created Them - Towards a Path of Dialogue on the Question of Gender Theory in Education' - the Vatican's educational document opposing 'gender theory', which it says 'denies the difference and reciprocity in nature of a man and a woman' and 'eliminat[es] the anthropological basis of the family'.
